note: Declares WHAT speech the game needs, not how it is made. The pipeline never discovers work by scanning code — if it is not declared here it is not generated. See tools/speech/README.md.

word.note: Every vocabulary word across all seven difficulty tiers. Only the 'word' field is read — the emoji is a picture hint on screen and never reaches a recording. Grapheme markers are stripped, so MOU[CH]A is recorded as moucha. Sent lowercase: an all-capitals word invites the model to spell it out.

master_format.note: What the provider returns and what is archived. Lossless, so the shipped bitrate can change without paying to resynthesise.

ship_format.note: What goes in the AAB. Revisit only after the Phase 3 A/B listening test on a TV.

processing.note: Any change here restages every clip for re-encoding, because it changes the audio — but only re-encoding, from the archived masters. It never costs a synthesis credit. Bump the version deliberately.
processing.levelling_note: Mean RMS with a peak ceiling, not EBU R128. Integrated loudness needs a window a letter name does not have — 'bé' is under 400ms and loudnorm measures it as -inf. One target for the whole voice family also keeps the batch consistent, which matters more here than any single clip hitting a number.

pricing_usd_per_1k_chars.note: Estimation only, for the plan report. RECHECK at https://elevenlabs.io/pricing/api before any production run — these change.

generate_guards.note: Refuses to spend more than this in one run unless the numbers are raised deliberately.

future_categories.note: Not generated yet, and reserved so the runtime can already resolve them. SpeechManager accepts an optional 'key' on any narration segment, so recording the menu and recap framing later is a data change rather than a code change — give the segment a key, add the category here, and it resolves.
future_categories.ui.recap.*: The finish-recap framing: 'you counted to', 'you collected the letters'. Spoken in the UI language, which is often not the learning language.
future_categories.ui.help.*: The 14 help slides. Long, rarely heard twice, and the least worthwhile to record.
